title: Offline-first SDK resume protocol and compatibility PRD
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Define a cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) PRD for an offline-first resume protocol that lets SDKs recover long-running streaming or paginated fetches after network interruptions or app restarts. Goals are to provide a secure, compact resume token format; clear backward-compatibility and downgrade paths for older SDKs; minimal runtime overhead; and documented migration and rollout guidance for customers.

Scope:
- Include streaming (server-sent partial responses / chunked tokens) and paginated fetches (cursor/offset-based) recovery semantics.
- Define resume token lifecycle, encryption/KMS binding, and expiry semantics.
- Define client storage recommendations (encrypted local storage, ephemeral memory), and when to persist vs ephemeral.
- Cross-SDK specification: examples and reference code in Python, TS, and Go.
- Acceptance tests, conformance harness, and compatibility matrix.

Out of scope:
- Full server-side session migration across regions (follow-up ENG epic).
- Offline compute or local LLM execution.

Success metrics:
- SDKs can resume >95% of interrupted sessions in lab network loss simulation.
- Security review completed and threat model mitigations accepted.
- Customer docs and migration guide published with examples for three client languages.
acceptance_criteria: Reference spec drafted and reviewed by Eng + Security + DX (docs) with sign-off
Compact resume token format defined (<=512 bytes) with version header and HMAC/AEAD; server rejects expired/invalid tokens
Reference implementations in Python/TS/Go that can: resume streaming chunks, resume paginated fetches, and fall back to full re-fetch when resume token rejected
Conformance test harness that simulates network dropout, token corruption, device restart, and succeeds >=95% resume rate in CI for non-adversarial cases
Backward compatibility: older SDKs without resume support gracefully downgrade to idempotent re-fetch and do not break APIs
Latency/regression: SDK runtime added overhead per request <5% median CPU/time in microbenchmarks
Security: security review completed with KMS binding and threat mitigations (replay, token theft) documented
Docs: migration guide, sample app for mobile (React Native), and API surface docs published in Console and SDK repos
Rollout: canary rollout plan exists with telemetry hooks to measure resume success and failure reasons
notes: 2026-03-10 Asha: Kickoff PRD draft. Key tradeoff between server-side sticky sessions vs client-provided resume tokens — prefer client tokens to avoid server state growth.
2026-03-11 Marco: Asked Eng to evaluate token size/serialization options (protobuf vs compact JSON) and local storage encryption approaches for mobile.
2026-03-12 Eng-8721: Prototype shows protobuf+lz4 yields ~120 bytes average token for common use; need AEAD wrapping for tamper resistance.

2026-03-12 Security: Flagged threat model: stolen device could replay resume token; recommendation to bind token to device fingerprint + short expiry and server-side revocation list for high-risk tokens.
2026-03-13 PM review: Add explicit fallback for older clients where server supplies simple page-token for compatibility; include migration doc examples.

2026-03-14 Design: Proposed SDK UX: expose ResumeHandle object with explicit persist()/forget() API; default: ephemeral in-memory until app background, optional persist flag for long-running user tasks.
Decision log: Use versioned opaque resume tokens with fields: version, model_id, route_hash, cursor_kv, expiry_ts, nonce; token sealed by server AEAD with KMS key id included in metadata.
Follow-ups: ENG epic to add server endpoints for token introspection and revocation will be created (ENG-9135).
